10.title: Two Ways of Seeing a River

sentences.text: The face of the water, in time, became a wonderful book—a book that was a dead language to the uneducated passenger, but which told its mind to me without reserve, delivering its most cherished secrets as clearly as if it uttered them with a voice.
sentences.translation: 渐渐地，水面变成了一本奇妙的书——对不懂领航的乘客来说，它如同一门无法理解的死语言；对我却毫无保留地袒露心意，清楚地传达最珍贵的秘密，仿佛真的开口说话一般。

classification.label: 主从复合句
classification.reason: 主句带有限定从句；按主干、从属关系和内部成分逐层拆解。
classification.note: 两个关系从句都修饰 book，不因第二个用 which 就变成主句。uneducated 在这里指未受水面解读训练；dead language 是难以读懂的比喻，不是断言乘客文盲。as if 用拟人情景说明清楚程度。

delivering …，逻辑主语是拟人化的 book
as if it uttered them with a voice

which told its mind to me without reserve,
as if it uttered them with a voice.
sentences.note: 两个关系从句都修饰 book，不因第二个用 which 就变成主句。uneducated 在这里指未受水面解读训练；dead language 是难以读懂的比喻，不是断言乘客文盲。as if 用拟人情景说明清楚程度。
sentences.paraphrase: The river became a readable source of information for the trained pilot, though ordinary passengers could not understand its language.

reuse.zh: 这座城市成了一本书——游客觉得陌生，却向居民讲述熟悉故事的一本书。
reuse.en: The city became a book—a book that seemed strange to visitors, but which told familiar stories to its residents.
reuse.note: 两个关系从句同修饰 book；先建立主干，再增加对照。

pdfNotes.title: 河面即书：全篇持续的比喻
pdfNotes.text: face、book、language、read、story 构成持续隐喻；后面的 page、italicized、capitals、exclamation points 都属于同一系统。书是河面，读者是领航员；uneducated 指没有受过这种解读训练，不等于一般文盲。

pdfNotes.title: 两个定语从句与一个分词补充
pdfNotes.text: a book 是前一 book 的同位说明；that was … 与 but which told … 同修饰这本书。delivering 延续拟人化的 book 的动作；as clearly as if … 比较传达秘密的清楚程度，不能误把 if 单列成现实条件。

sentences.text: And it was not a book to be read once and thrown aside, for it had a new story to tell every day.
sentences.translation: 而这并不是读一遍就可以扔到一边的书，因为它每天都有一个新故事可讲。

classification.label: 并列句
classification.reason: 两个或以上并列主句，各自具有主语与限定谓语。
classification.note: for 在这里作为并列连词补充原因；read 与 thrown 共用 to be。story to tell 用主动形式表达待讲述内容，不能因此一律改 to be told。

clauses: to be read once and [to be] thrown aside
it had a new story to tell every day
functions: to be read once and thrown aside,
sentences.note: for 在这里作为并列连词补充原因；read 与 thrown 共用 to be。story to tell 用主动形式表达待讲述内容，不能因此一律改 to be told。
sentences.paraphrase: The river offered fresh information every day, so it could never be read once and dismissed.

reuse.pattern: It was not ___ to be ___, for it had ___.
reuse.zh: 这不是一份可以随手忽略的报告，因为它包含重要证据。
reuse.en: It was not a report to be casually ignored, for it had important evidence.
reuse.note: to be done 作后置定语；for 后接完整主句说明原因。

pdfNotes.title: 河面即书：全篇持续的比喻
pdfNotes.text: face、book、language、read、story 构成持续隐喻；后面的 page、italicized、capitals、exclamation points 都属于同一系统。书是河面，读者是领航员；uneducated 指没有受过这种解读训练，不等于一般文盲。

pdfNotes.title: for 连接主句，两个不定式各有功能
pdfNotes.text: for 用并列连词说明原因。to be read once and thrown aside 是 book 的被动不定式定语，thrown 共用 to be；a new story to tell 中 to tell 则是主动形式修饰待讲的故事，不应见主动形式就改错。

sentences.text: Throughout the long twelve hundred miles there was never a page that was void of interest, never one that you could leave unread without loss, never one that you would want to skip, thinking you could find higher enjoyment in some other thing.
sentences.translation: 在漫长的一千二百英里河段上，从没有一页缺乏趣味；没有一页可以不读而不损失什么；也没有一页会让你想跳过，以为别处能找到更大的乐趣。

classification.label: 并列复合句
classification.reason: 同时包含主句之间的并列以及内部或附加的限定从句。
classification.note: one 替代 page；后两组压缩重复的 there was，形成排比。leave 的宾语由 that 对应 page，unread 为宾补；thinking 的人是 you，不是 page。

clauses: [there was] never one … / [there was] never one …
that you could leave unread without loss
that you would want to skip
thinking [that] you could find …，隐含主语 you
functions: Throughout the long twelve hundred miles
that you could leave unread without loss,
that you would want to skip,
you could find higher enjoyment in some other thing.
sentences.note: one 替代 page；后两组压缩重复的 there was，形成排比。leave 的宾语由 that 对应 page，unread 为宾补；thinking 的人是 you，不是 page。
sentences.paraphrase: Every part of the river held interest, and skipping any part meant missing something worthwhile.

reuse.pattern: There was never a ___ that ___, never one that ___.
reuse.zh: 从没有哪一章毫无意义，也没有哪一章可以跳过而不失去什么。
reuse.en: There was never a chapter that lacked meaning, never one that could be skipped without loss.
reuse.note: never one 延续省略的 there was，one 替代 chapter。

pdfNotes.title: 排比省略与真正的 thinking 主语
pdfNotes.text: 讲义的连词省略提示有帮助；never one 重复 page，并压缩 there was。thinking 的隐含主语是从句里的 you，后接省略 that 的内容从句；不是说书页在思考。leave [page] unread 为宾语加宾补。

pdfNotes.title: void 与 never 的否定范围
pdfNotes.text: never a page that was void of interest 等于没有任何一页毫无趣味；never … without loss 表跳过就会有损失。twelve hundred 为一千二百，本文的航段尺度不能当作整条河流的精确长度资料。

sentences.text: There never was so wonderful a book written by man; never one whose interest was so absorbing, so unflagging, so sparkingly renewed with every re-perusal.
sentences.translation: 人类从未写出过这样奇妙的书；也从未有哪本书如此引人入胜，趣味毫不衰减，每次重读都焕发鲜活光彩。

classification.label: 并列复合句
classification.reason: 同时包含主句之间的并列以及内部或附加的限定从句。
classification.note: so + 形容词 + a + 单数名词：so wonderful a book。whose 表所属，interest 是从句主语。sparkingly 的版本拼写与所核电子原书一致，保留并释为鲜活焕新，不把它作为普通现代副词强行背记。

clauses: There never was so wonderful a book …
whose interest was so absorbing, so unflagging, so sparkingly renewed …
functions: so sparkingly renewed with every re-perusal.
sentences.note: so + 形容词 + a + 单数名词：so wonderful a book。whose 表所属，interest 是从句主语。sparkingly 的版本拼写与所核电子原书一致，保留并释为鲜活焕新，不把它作为普通现代副词强行背记。
sentences.paraphrase: No human-written book offered such absorbing and endlessly renewed interest.

reuse.pattern: There never was so ___ a ___ as ___.
reuse.zh: 从没有哪幅景象像那次落日一样鲜活。
reuse.en: There never was so vivid a scene as that sunset.
reuse.note: so + 形容词 + a + 单数名词；也可用 such a vivid scene 改写。

pdfNotes.title: so wonderful a book 与 whose
pdfNotes.text: so 修饰形容词时可用 so + adjective + a/an + 单数名词；不要机械改为 so a wonderful book。分号后省略 there never was；whose 说明 book 与 interest 的所属关系，interest 作从句主语。

pdfNotes.title: 保留 sparkingly 的版本拼写
pdfNotes.text: 所给两份 PDF 的本文段落与所核 Project Gutenberg 第 9 章均作 sparkingly，不据现代常见 sparklingly 就静默改原句。这里按每次重读都重新焕发鲜活光彩理解；不把这个罕见版本形式列作现代高频主动词汇。若需做校勘，仍应另比印本。

references.label: Mark Twain · Life on the Mississippi, Chapter 9

sentences.text: The passenger who could not read it was charmed with a peculiar sort of faint dimple on its surface (on the rare occasions when he did not overlook it altogether); but to the pilot that was an italicized passage; indeed, it was more than that, it was a legend of the largest capitals, with a string of shouting exclamation points at the end of it; for it meant that a wreck or a rock was buried there that could tear the life out of the strongest vessel that ever floated.
sentences.translation: 不懂读这本书的乘客，偶尔没把水面那一丝特别的“酒窝”完全忽略时，会觉得它迷人；领航员看见的却是一段斜体强调文字，甚至不止如此，而是用最大号大写字母写成、末尾带一串高喊的感叹号的警示；因为那说明水下埋着沉船或岩石，足以撕毁最坚固的船。

classification.label: 并列复合句
classification.reason: 同时包含主句之间的并列以及内部或附加的限定从句。
classification.note: 警示的升级链是 italicized passage → legend in capitals → shouting exclamation points。there 后的 that 从句因较长而后移，修饰 wreck/rock，不修饰 there；末尾 that 才修饰 vessel。文学并置的逗号不作为现代正式写作任意连接主句的通用规则。

who could not read it 修饰 passenger
when he did not overlook it … 修饰 occasions
but … that was an italicized passage
it was more than that / it was a legend …
that a wreck or a rock was buried there …
that could tear … 修饰 a wreck or a rock
that ever floated 修饰 vessel
functions: with a peculiar sort of faint dimple on its surface
when he did not overlook it altogether);
a legend of the largest capitals,
with a string of shouting exclamation points at the end of it;
that could tear the life out of the strongest vessel
sentences.note: 警示的升级链是 italicized passage → legend in capitals → shouting exclamation points。there 后的 that 从句因较长而后移，修饰 wreck/rock，不修饰 there；末尾 that 才修饰 vessel。文学并置的逗号不作为现代正式写作任意连接主句的通用规则。
sentences.paraphrase: A tiny surface mark charmed passengers but warned pilots of a deadly underwater obstacle.

reuse.pattern: To ___, it was ___; to ___, it was ___.
reuse.zh: 在游客眼中它是一道美丽波纹；在领航员眼中它是一则紧急警告。
reuse.en: To the visitor, it was a beautiful ripple; to the pilot, it was an urgent warning.
reuse.note: 两端用相同主句骨架体现视角变化，分号连接完整主句。

pdfNotes.title: 关系从句后移，不是修饰 there
pdfNotes.text: a wreck or a rock was buried there that could tear … 中，长 that 从句后移，先行词仍是 wreck/rock。讲义所注 end-weight 有助理解这种后置。末尾 that ever floated 则修饰 vessel，两层先行词不同。

pdfNotes.title: 字体与警告层层加强
pdfNotes.text: italicized passage → largest capitals → shouting exclamation points，把微小水纹的危险性写成越来越醒目的警告。legend 在此为说明文字，capital 为大写字母；hideous 描写专业读者感到的危险，不单是外观丑陋。

pdfNotes.title: 文学并置不等于随意逗号拼句
pdfNotes.text: 讲义在 it was more than that, it was a legend … 之间补 and，是一种展开阅读办法。这里原文以文学并置增强节奏；现代正式写作可用分号、句号或合适连词，不能推出任意两主句都可只用逗号连接。

sentences.text: It is the faintest and simplest expression the water ever makes, and the most hideous to a pilot's eye.
sentences.translation: 这是水面能作出的最微弱、最简单的表达，却也是领航员眼中最骇人的。

classification.label: 主从复合句
classification.reason: 主句带有限定从句；按主干、从属关系和内部成分逐层拆解。
classification.note: 定语从句缺 makes 的宾语，因此省略的是关系词 that。and 后省略 expression；最微弱的迹象也可能传达最大的危险。

clauses: It is the faintest and simplest expression … and the most hideous [expression]
省略关系词的定语从句
sentences.note: 定语从句缺 makes 的宾语，因此省略的是关系词 that。and 后省略 expression；最微弱的迹象也可能传达最大的危险。
sentences.paraphrase: The smallest water signal could also be the most alarming to a pilot.

reuse.pattern: It is the ___ that ___, and the most ___ to ___.
reuse.zh: 这是最容易被忽略的细节，却也是研究者眼中最有价值的。
reuse.en: It is the detail that is easiest to overlook, and the most valuable to a researcher.
reuse.note: and 后省略重复的 detail；to a researcher 说明评价角度。

pdfNotes.title: 字体与警告层层加强
pdfNotes.text: italicized passage → largest capitals → shouting exclamation points，把微小水纹的危险性写成越来越醒目的警告。legend 在此为说明文字，capital 为大写字母；hideous 描写专业读者感到的危险，不单是外观丑陋。

pdfNotes.title: 省略的关系词与省略的中心名词
pdfNotes.text: expression [that] the water ever makes 中，关系词作 makes 的宾语而省略。and the most hideous 后省略 expression，仍与 faintest、simplest 构成表语评价，不是另一个完整限定主句。

sentences.text: In truth, the passenger who could not read this book saw nothing but all manner of pretty pictures in it, painted by the sun and shaded by the clouds, whereas to the trained eye these were not pictures at all, but the grimmest and most dead-earnest of reading matter.
sentences.translation: 事实上，读不懂这本书的乘客只看见种种漂亮画面，由阳光上色、云影铺阴；受过训练的人眼中，那根本不是图画，而是最严峻、最不可儿戏的阅读材料。

classification.label: 主从复合句
classification.reason: 主句带有限定从句；按主干、从属关系和内部成分逐层拆解。
classification.note: nothing but 表“只有”；whereas 引出对照，教学按从属对照从句分析。trained eye 借眼睛指专业观察者；reading matter 是阅读材料，matter 不译为“问题”。

clauses: the passenger … saw nothing but … pictures
who could not read this book
painted … and shaded … 描写 pictures
whereas … these were not pictures … but … reading matter
functions: who could not read this book
nothing but all manner of pretty pictures in it,
not pictures at all, but the grimmest and most dead-earnest of reading matter.
sentences.note: nothing but 表“只有”；whereas 引出对照，教学按从属对照从句分析。trained eye 借眼睛指专业观察者；reading matter 是阅读材料，matter 不译为“问题”。
sentences.paraphrase: Passengers enjoyed attractive images, whereas pilots read serious practical warnings.

reuse.pattern: ___ saw nothing but ___, whereas to ___ these were ___.
reuse.zh: 游客只看到装饰图案，历史学家看到的却是过去的证据。
reuse.en: Visitors saw nothing but decorative patterns, whereas to historians these were evidence of the past.
reuse.note: nothing but 表只有；whereas 对照两种解释。

pdfNotes.title: whereas 的对照与分词指向
pdfNotes.text: whereas 引出对照从句，连接乘客和专业读者两种解读；painted by the sun 与 shaded by the clouds 都描写 pictures。nothing but 是只有，not … but … 则是“不是……而是……”，两处 but 功能不同。

pdfNotes.title: trained eye 与 reading matter
pdfNotes.text: trained eye 借眼睛指有训练的观察者；reading matter 是阅读材料，matter 通常不可数。dead-earnest 在此表示极其严肃、不可儿戏，不是死人在认真读书。

sentences.text: Now when I had mastered the language of this water and had come to know every trifling feature that bordered the great river as familiarly as I knew the letters of the alphabet, I had made a valuable acquisition.
sentences.translation: 当我掌握了河水的语言，熟悉大河沿岸每一个微小特征，就像熟悉字母表那样时，我已经获得了一项宝贵本领。

classification.label: 主从复合句
classification.reason: 主句带有限定从句；按主干、从属关系和内部成分逐层拆解。
classification.note: as familiarly as … 对应 come to know，不是修饰 bordered。长 when 从句结束后，主句 I had made 才出现；过去完成时服务于回忆的时间层次。

clauses: when I had mastered … and had come to know …
that bordered the great river 修饰 feature
as familiarly as I knew the letters of the alphabet，修饰 had come to know
as I knew the letters of the alphabet
I had made a valuable acquisition
functions: as I knew the letters of the alphabet,
sentences.note: 定语从句止于 that bordered the great river。as familiarly as … 修饰 had come to know，其中比较从句为 as I knew the letters of the alphabet。
sentences.paraphrase: Knowing the river as intimately as the alphabet gave the narrator a valuable skill.

reuse.pattern: When I had learned ___ as well as I knew ___, I had gained ___.
reuse.zh: 当我像熟悉自家街道一样熟悉路线时，我就掌握了一项有用的本领。
reuse.en: When I had learned the route as well as I knew my own street, I had gained a useful skill.
reuse.note: as well as 在此比较熟悉程度；不是“以及”的追加用法。

pdfNotes.title: 比较的对象是熟悉程度
pdfNotes.text: as familiarly as I knew the letters … 修饰 come to know 的方式程度，不接到 bordered 上。when 从句内部 had mastered 与 had come to know 并列，外层主句到第二个 I had made 才开始。

pdfNotes.title: 有所得，也有所失
pdfNotes.text: acquisition 指掌握河道知识的宝贵收获；lost something 由后文 grace、beauty、poetry 具体展开。作者的失去是审美体验变化，不是说知识毫无价值，或河流外观实际发生了同样的消失。

sentences.text: But I had lost something, too.
sentences.translation: 但我也失去了一些东西。

classification.label: 简单句

classification.note: had lost 为过去完成时，承接掌握本领后的反思；too 放句末，表示有所得同时有所失。

sentences.note: had lost 为过去完成时，承接掌握本领后的反思；too 放句末，表示有所得同时有所失。
sentences.paraphrase: The new skill came with a loss.

reuse.zh: 但我也失去了最初的新鲜感。
reuse.en: But I had lost my initial sense of novelty, too.
reuse.note: 过去完成时与前文获得技能的回忆层次配合。

pdfNotes.title: 有所得，也有所失
pdfNotes.text: acquisition 指掌握河道知识的宝贵收获；lost something 由后文 grace、beauty、poetry 具体展开。作者的失去是审美体验变化，不是说知识毫无价值，或河流外观实际发生了同样的消失。

sentences.text: I had lost something which could never be restored to me while I lived.
sentences.translation: 我失去的东西，在有生之年再也无法恢复。

classification.label: 主从复合句
classification.reason: 主句带有限定从句；按主干、从属关系和内部成分逐层拆解。
classification.note: which 作被动从句主语，指失去的东西；restore something to someone。while I lived 意为在余生，不是“虽然我活着”的让步。

clauses: which could never be restored to me …

reuse.zh: 我失去了一次在那份工作期间再也无法获得的机会。
reuse.en: I had lost an opportunity which could never be regained while I remained in that job.
reuse.note: which 作被动从句主语；while 再限定时间。

pdfNotes.text: acquisition 指掌握河道知识的宝贵收获；lost something 由后文 grace、beauty、poetry 具体展开。作者的失去是审美体验变化，不是说知识毫无价值，或河流外观实际发生了同样的消失。

pdfNotes.title: 嵌套从句与长宾语后放

sentences.text: A broad expanse of the river was turned to blood; in the middle distance the red hue brightened into gold, through which a solitary log came floating, black and conspicuous; in one place a long, slanting mark lay sparkling upon the water; in another the surface was broken by boiling, tumbling rings, that were as many-tinted as an opal; where the ruddy flush was faintest, was a smooth spot that was covered with graceful circles and radiating lines, ever so delicately traced; the shore on our left was densely wooded, and the somber shadow that fell from this forest was broken in one place by a long, ruffled trail that shone like silver; and high above the forest wall a clean-stemmed dead tree waved a single leafy bough that glowed like a flame in the unobstructed splendor that was flowing from the sun.
sentences.translation: 宽阔河面染成血红；中景的红色转为金色，一根孤零零的木头从中漂来，黑而显眼；一处细长的斜纹在水上闪光；另一处水面被翻滚的环纹打破，色彩像欧泊般变幻；红晕最淡处是一片平滑水面，优美圆纹和放射线被极细致地勾勒其上；左岸林木茂密，投下的阴影中有一道皱褶般的长水痕闪着银光；林墙高处，一株光秃的枯树挥动唯一带叶的大枝，在太阳无遮无挡的灿烂光辉中像火焰般发亮。

sentences.text: Then, if that sunset scene had been repeated, I should have looked upon it without rapture, and should have commented upon it, inwardly, after this fashion: This sun means that we are going to have wind tomorrow; that floating log means that the river is rising, small thanks to it; that slanting mark on the water refers to a bluff reef which is going to kill somebody's steamboat one of these nights, if it keeps on stretching out like that; those tumbling "boils" show a dissolving bar and a changing channel there; the lines and circles in the slick water over yonder are a warning that that troublesome place is shoaling up dangerously; that silver streak in the shadow of the forest is the "break" from a new snag, and he has located himself in the very best place he could have found to fish for steamboats; that tall dead tree, with a single living branch, is not going to last long, and then how is a body ever going to get through this blind place at night without the friendly old landmark.
sentences.translation: 那时，如果那场落日重现，我也不会再陶醉，只会在心里这样评论：这太阳说明明天有风；漂木说明涨水，真没什么可高兴的；水上斜纹提示有陡直沙脊，如果继续延伸，哪天夜里就会毁掉一艘汽船；翻涌的“沸泡”说明沙洲在被冲散、航道在改变；那边平滑水上的线圈警告那处麻烦地方正危险地变浅；林影中的银纹是新枯木激起的水面扰动，它简直选中了捕捉汽船的最佳位置；那棵只剩一根活枝的高枯树也撑不了多久，到时少了这位友善的老地标，夜里还怎么驶过这段难辨的水路呢。

pdfNotes.title: bluff reef 的前文说明：这里有沙脊
pdfNotes.text: 原书第 9 章在选段之前明确解释，bluff reef 下方有侧面近乎房墙般陡直的 solid sand-bar。因此本篇译成陡直水下沙脊，比一概套“珊瑚礁”或岩石礁准确；reef 的范围可包括沙脊。

pdfNotes.title: snag 与 he 的拟人化
pdfNotes.text: snag 在此为嵌入河床、威胁船只的木头；he 和 himself 回指它。fish for steamboats 把木头拟作等待“钓船”的人，kill a steamboat 也指毁船，不一定是人的死亡。small thanks to it 是对涨水的讽刺评语。

pdfNotes.title: boils、break、body 不按最熟悉义项套
pdfNotes.text: boils 是翻涌的水泡状环纹，不是皮肤疖子；break 为水下障碍引起的水面扰动，不是休息。a body 是旧式口语的“人”，landmark 指导航地标；blind place 是夜间难辨的水路。

sentences.text: No, the romance and the beauty were all gone from the river.
sentences.translation: 不，河流的浪漫情趣和美已经全消失了。

classification.label: 简单句
classification.reason: 一个展开的限定主句；共用主语的并列谓语、非谓语或缩略表达另作提示。
classification.note: were gone 表“已经不在”的状态，不是把不及物 go 硬分析成被动。romance 在此指诗意和神秘情趣，而非恋情。

clauses: the romance and the beauty were all gone from the river
sentences.note: were gone 表“已经不在”的状态，不是把不及物 go 硬分析成被动。romance 在此指诗意和神秘情趣，而非恋情。
sentences.paraphrase: The river had lost its imaginative and aesthetic appeal for the narrator.

reuse.pattern: The ___ and the ___ were all gone from ___.
reuse.zh: 这封信里的温暖和信任已经全消失了。
reuse.en: The warmth and the trust were all gone from the letter.
reuse.note: were gone 描写结果状态；并列主语配 were。

pdfNotes.title: were gone 与两个省略关系词
pdfNotes.text: were gone 描述已经消失的状态，并非 go 的被动。All the value [that] any feature … had … was … usefulness [that] it could furnish … 中，两处关系词都是宾语可省略；主句 value was usefulness 必须跨过内部从句识别。

sentences.text: All the value any feature of it had for me now was the amount of usefulness it could furnish toward compassing the safe piloting of a steamboat.
sentences.translation: 如今，河流任何特征对我的全部价值，都只在于它能为实现汽船安全领航提供多少实际帮助。

classification.label: 主从复合句
classification.reason: 主句带有限定从句；按主干、从属关系和内部成分逐层拆解。
classification.note: 两个关系词都作宾语而省略；外层主干不是 any feature had …，要跨到 was。前 it 指 river，后 it 指 any feature；compass 是旧式“实现”，toward 后接 -ing。

clauses: All the value … was the amount of usefulness …
[that] any feature of it had for me now 修饰 value
[that] it could furnish … 修饰 usefulness
toward compassing the safe piloting of a steamboat
functions: toward compassing the safe piloting of a steamboat.
sentences.note: 两个关系词都作宾语而省略；外层主干不是 any feature had …，要跨到 was。前 it 指 river，后 it 指 any feature；compass 是旧式“实现”，toward 后接 -ing。
sentences.paraphrase: He now valued river features only for their practical contribution to safe navigation.

reuse.pattern: All the value ___ had for me was the ___ it could ___.
reuse.zh: 这个工具对我的全部价值，就是它能节省的时间。
reuse.en: All the value the tool had for me was the time it could save.
reuse.note: value 后省略关系词，time 后也省略作 save 宾语的关系词；外层 value was time。

pdfNotes.title: compass 不是拿指南针指路
pdfNotes.text: toward compassing the safe piloting … 中 compass 是旧式及物动词“实现”，后面宾语是安全领航这件事；toward 为介词所以用 -ing。Cambridge 常用名词与 Merriam-Webster 动词释义并列标明，避免把词性查漏。

sentences.text: Since those days, I have pitied doctors from my heart.
sentences.translation: 从那以后，我由衷地同情医生。

classification.label: 简单句
classification.reason: 一个展开的限定主句；共用主语的并列谓语、非谓语或缩略表达另作提示。
classification.note: Since 后接名词短语，不构成从句；主句现在完成时连接过去到叙述当下。后文用医生作类比，非职业事实调查。

sentences.paraphrase: This experience made him feel sincere sympathy for doctors.

reuse.pattern: Since ___, I have ___ from my heart.
reuse.zh: 从那以后，我一直由衷地敬佩他们。
reuse.en: Since that day, I have admired them from my heart.
reuse.note: since + 过去起点，主句现在完成时；这是稳定的时态结构。

pdfNotes.title: 医生类比保留作者的反问
pdfNotes.text: 作者把领航员从美景读出危险，类比医生从容貌看出病征。它提出专业知识所得与审美所失的张力，不是证明所有医生都会失去审美，也不是对某位人物作实际诊断。正文的偏向性问句需要与事实陈述区分。

sentences.text: What does the lovely flush in a beauty's cheek mean to a doctor but a "break" that ripples above some deadly disease?
sentences.translation: 美人脸颊上可爱的红晕，对医生来说，除了像水下致命危险之上的一道水纹，还能意味着什么呢？

classification.label: 主从复合句
classification.reason: 主句带有限定从句；按主干、从属关系和内部成分逐层拆解。
classification.note: What … but …? 为“除了……还能是什么”的反问。break 承接上文枯木激起的表面扰动，比喻表象下的危险；不是休息时间。专用 PDF 漏句末标点，网页保留问号便于阅读。

that ripples above some deadly disease 修饰 break

that ripples above some deadly disease?

sentences.paraphrase: He imagines a doctor reading a beautiful blush as a warning of hidden illness.

reuse.zh: 对于水手来说，灯塔除了意味着希望，还能意味着什么呢？
reuse.en: What does a lighthouse mean to a sailor but hope?
reuse.note: What … but …? 用反问强调说话者认定的答案，不是中性信息提问。

pdfNotes.text: What … mean … but …? 是除了这个还能意味着什么的反问。第 24 句 with 后的 what are … 既有名词性指代又有内部关系功能，相当于 the things which are …；are 可对应复数 signs and symbols，不能机械要求 what 一律配 is。

pdfNotes.title: 专用 PDF 的句末标点
pdfNotes.text: 专用讲义第 23 句没有句末标点，网页已有问号；所核电子原书该处用句点，但句法仍是 What does …? 的反问结构。保留网页便于教学的问号，并明确这是版本标点差别，不改动音频文字。

sentences.text: Are not all her visible charms sown thick with what are to him the signs and symbols of hidden decay?
sentences.translation: 她身上一切看得见的魅力，难道不都密布着在他眼中代表潜在病变的迹象和符号吗？

classification.label: 主从复合句
classification.reason: 主句带有限定从句；按主干、从属关系和内部成分逐层拆解。
classification.note: with 后的 what 结构整体作介词宾语，what 内部对应多种 signs and symbols，故可用 are。sown thick 是“密布”的比喻；不由 are 就推断 what 必须单数。

what are to him the signs and symbols of hidden decay

sentences.paraphrase: He asks whether a doctor sees apparent beauty as a collection of diagnostic signs.

reuse.pattern: Are not ___ filled with what are to ___ ___?
reuse.zh: 这些旧照片难道不充满了对她而言最珍贵的记忆吗？
reuse.en: Are not these old photographs filled with what are to her the most precious memories?
reuse.note: what 结构作 with 的宾语，内部为复数意义；普通语序也可用 Aren't these …?。

sentences.text: Does he ever see her beauty at all, or doesn't he simply view her professionally, and comment upon her unwholesome condition all to himself?
sentences.translation: 他究竟还看得到她的美吗？还是只从专业角度审视她，在心里独自评论她的不健康状况？

classification.label: 并列句
classification.reason: 两个或以上并列主句，各自具有主语与限定谓语。
classification.note: or 连接两套反问；第二问里的 and 只并列 view、comment。to himself 表在心里，并不真的对病人说出这些话；否定问式带作者倾向，不是已证明的普遍结论。

clauses: Does he ever see her beauty at all?
doesn't he simply view her professionally and [doesn't he] comment …?
view 与 comment 共用 he 和助动词框架
sentences.note: or 连接两套反问；第二问里的 and 只并列 view、comment。to himself 表在心里，并不真的对病人说出这些话；否定问式带作者倾向，不是已证明的普遍结论。
sentences.paraphrase: He wonders whether professional examination has displaced the doctor's appreciation of beauty.

pdfNotes.title: 外层倒装，whether 内不倒装
pdfNotes.text: 第 25 句 or 连接两组疑问，第二组 view 与 comment 共用主语。第 26 句 whether 内仍用 he has gained … or [has] lost … 的陈述语序；most 对举所获与所失，现代改写可用 more，不把它强译成与所有人相比最多。

sentences.text: And doesn't he sometimes wonder whether he has gained most or lost most by learning his trade?
sentences.translation: 他难道不会有时也想，学会了这门职业，究竟得到的更多，还是失去的更多？

classification.label: 主从复合句
classification.reason: 主句带有限定从句；按主干、从属关系和内部成分逐层拆解。
classification.note: whether 从句用陈述语序；lost 前可补 has。原文用 most 对举所得所失，现代转述可写 gained more or lost more；不要把 most 生硬译成“所有人中最多”。结尾保留得失之问。

clauses: whether he has gained most or [has] lost most …
sentences.note: whether 从句用陈述语序；lost 前可补 has。原文用 most 对举所得所失，现代转述可写 gained more or lost more；不要把 most 生硬译成“所有人中最多”。结尾保留得失之问。
sentences.paraphrase: He leaves open the question of whether learning a profession brings more gain or more loss.

reuse.pattern: Doesn't ___ sometimes wonder whether ___ has ___ or ___?
reuse.zh: 她难道不会有时也想，这次变化究竟帮了自己还是妨碍了自己？
reuse.en: Doesn't she sometimes wonder whether the change has helped her or hindered her?
reuse.note: 外层疑问倒装，whether 内仍为陈述语序；hindered 共用 has。

vocabulary.definition: lacking something completely — 完全缺乏……的
collocations: void of interest 毫无趣味的
void of meaning 没有意义的
void of emotion 毫无感情的
compare: void of：强调完全没有，语气书面
devoid of：相近的书面表达
free of：不含某物，常强调摆脱不想要的东西
lacking in：某方面不足，未必全无
vocabulary.usage: 原文 never a page that was void of interest 意为每一页都有意思；never 与 void 的否定结合，不能译成“每页都没趣”。固定 of。

vocabulary.definition: never weakening in energy, interest or effort — 不减弱的；持久不懈的
collocations: unflagging enthusiasm 持久的热情
unflagging support 始终如一的支持
unflagging energy 不减的精力
compare: unflagging：关注强度没有衰减
unwavering：立场或决心不动摇
tireless：做事仿佛不疲倦
constant：一直存在，未必精力充沛
vocabulary.usage: 来自 flag 的“衰退”义，不是“没有旗帜”。原文 interest 指这本“河流之书”的吸引力持续不减。

vocabulary.definition: the act of reading or looking through something — 阅读；阅览
collocations: for your perusal 供您阅览
a careful perusal 仔细阅读
a quick perusal 快速翻阅
compare: perusal：较正式的阅读、查阅，不自动保证精读
study：以理解或研究为目的深入学习
skim：快速抓大意
scan：为寻找特定信息扫读
vocabulary.usage: 原文 re-perusal 加 re- 表再次阅读。不能只凭 perusal 就断言“一定逐字精读”；程度由 careful、quick 等语境说明。

vocabulary.definition: weak or difficult to notice clearly — 微弱的；不明显的
collocations: a faint sound 微弱的声音
a faint glow 微光
a faint dimple 轻微的凹纹
compare: faint：强度低、不易察觉
vague：信息轮廓不明确
dim：光线昏暗
slight：程度或数量少，范围更广
vocabulary.usage: 本文修饰 dimple，并不是水面要晕倒。the faintest 为最高级；not have the faintest idea 表一点也不知道。
otherSenses: feel faint 感到要晕过去

vocabulary.definition: a small hollow in a surface — 小凹陷；本文为水面细小的凹纹
collocations: a dimple in one's cheek 面颊酒窝
a dimple on the surface 表面的小凹痕
dimpled cheeks 有酒窝的脸颊
compare: dimple：圆浅的小凹处，常让人联想到酒窝
dent：物体受压或撞击后的凹痕
ripple：水面的小波纹，不一定有凹陷形状
family: dimpled adj. 有酒窝或凹痕的
vocabulary.usage: 这里把水面写成有“酒窝”的脸，延续 face of the water；但它也是领航员识别水下障碍的迹象。不要只记人体义。
otherSenses: 人笑时脸颊或下巴上的酒窝

vocabulary.definition: to print or write in sloping type — 用斜体排印；以斜体突出
collocations: italicize a word 把单词设为斜体
an italicized passage 斜体段落
words in italics 斜体文字
compare: italicize：改变为斜体
underline：在下方画线
capitalize：用大写字母
highlight：使醒目，方法不限
vocabulary.usage: 英式也常拼 italicise。水面不是实际有印刷字，而是比喻细微水纹对专业读者具有强调作用。

vocabulary.definition: words on an object or image that identify or explain it — 题字；说明文字
collocations: a map legend 地图图例
a legend on a coin 钱币上的铭文
bear a legend 带有题字
compare: legend：附在物件、图像上的说明
caption：图片下面或旁边的文字
inscription：刻写在物体上的文字
myth：神话或流行误解，不是本文义
family: legend n. 传说；传奇人物；题字
vocabulary.usage: 这里 a legend of the largest capitals 是以巨大大写字母呈现的警示文字，不是“最大的首都传说”。与 book、italicized、exclamation points 同属阅读隐喻。
otherSenses: 地图上解释符号的图例

vocabulary.definition: a letter in its uppercase form — 大写字母
collocations: write in capitals 用大写字母写
a capital letter 大写字母
start with a capital 首字母大写
compare: capital：大写字母，也叫 uppercase letter
lowercase：小写形式
italic：斜体，与大小写是不同维度

vocabulary.definition: the punctuation mark ! used for forceful expression — 感叹号
collocations: an exclamation point 一个感叹号
a string of exclamation points 一连串感叹号

compare: exclamation point：标点符号“!”
exclamation：惊呼或感叹的话
question mark：问号，标示疑问
full stop：句号，表示句子结束

vocabulary.definition: extremely ugly, unpleasant or shocking — 丑陋可怕的；骇人的
collocations: a hideous sight 骇人的景象
a hideous mistake 极其糟糕的错误
look hideous 难看极了
compare: hideous：视觉或感受令人强烈反感、震惊
ugly：主要评价外观或丑恶性质
dangerous：会造成伤害，不一定看起来难看
grim：让人严肃忧虑、看到坏结果
family: hideously adv. 极其难看地；骇人地
vocabulary.usage: 对领航员而言 hideous 重点在细纹意味着严重危险，不是它在颜色形状上特别丑。the most hideous 后省略重复的 expression。

vocabulary.definition: used to stress what is actually true — 事实上；说真的
collocations: in truth, … 事实上……
but in truth … 但实际……
compare: in truth：强调真实情况，书面感较强
in fact：常用来补充或纠正事实
to be honest：突出说话人坦诚表达意见，不保证是在纠正事实
vocabulary.usage: 作为整句评注，通常不带 the。本文引出乘客与领航员的视角对照，而不是“在真理里面”。

vocabulary.definition: serious and worrying, often because danger or suffering is involved — 严峻的；令人忧惧的
collocations: a grim warning 严厉可怕的警告
a grim reality 严酷现实
a grim expression 严肃忧虑的神情
compare: grim：看到危险或坏前景而严峻
serious：郑重或重大，不必悲观
gloomy：情绪低落或前景黯淡
hideous：强烈难看或骇人
vocabulary.usage: 比较级 grimmer、最高级 grimmest，双写 m。本文 the grimmest … of reading matter 指最严峻的解读材料，不是“最阴沉的读书人”。

vocabulary.definition: small or seemingly unimportant — 微小的；看似微不足道的
collocations: a trifling detail 微小细节
a trifling sum 很小一笔钱
a trifling matter 小事
compare: trifling：重要性或数量小，常淡化分量
tiny：尺寸非常小
trivial：次要而不值得重视
subtle：细微不易察觉，可能很重要
family: trifle v. 轻率对待（常用 trifle with）
vocabulary.usage: 原文虽说 trifling feature，这些细节对航行可能重要，不能理解成“不值得学”。every 后用单数 feature。

vocabulary.definition: the ordered set of letters used to write a language — 字母表
collocations: the letters of the alphabet 字母表中的字母
the English alphabet 英文字母表
in alphabetical order 按字母顺序
compare: alphabet：整套按序字母
letter：其中一个字母
character：文字系统中的单个符号，范围比字母广
family: alphabetical adj. 按字母顺序的
alphabetically adv. 按字母顺序地
vocabulary.usage: 一个 a、b 是 a letter，不是 an alphabet。本文用熟悉字母表比喻对河道细节的熟悉。

vocabulary.definition: something valuable gained or learned — 获得的东西；本文为掌握河道知识的收获
collocations: a valuable acquisition 一项宝贵收获
the acquisition of knowledge 知识的获得
language acquisition 语言习得
compare: acquisition：获得的过程或成果
achievement：通过努力完成的成就
possession：拥有状态或所有物，不强调如何获得
learning：学习过程及知识
vocabulary.usage: a valuable acquisition 把知识技能看作一项收获；不能机械译为收购了一家公司。过程义常不可数，具体收获可数。

vocabulary.definition: impressive through great size, beauty or power — 雄伟的；壮丽庄严的
collocations: a majestic river 雄伟的大河
majestic mountains 壮丽山峦
majestic scenery 壮丽景色
compare: majestic：宏大、庄严，令人敬畏
beautiful：美的一般评价
grand：规模或气派宏大
picturesque：像画一样宜人，不必宏伟
vocabulary.usage: 原文对大河的客观称呼仍是 majestic；“美消失”讲的是作者体验的变化，不是河流实际失去体积或壮观形态。

vocabulary.definition: a broad open area of land, water or sky — 广阔的一片
collocations: a broad expanse of water 广阔的水面
a vast expanse of sky 辽阔天空
an expanse of grassland 一大片草原
compare: expanse：重在开阔延伸的空间
area：区域的中性称呼
extent：程度或延伸范围，不一定是眼前的一片景象
family: expansive adj. 广阔的；开朗健谈的
vocabulary.usage: a broad expanse of the river 指宽阔河面的一大片。不要误写为 expense（费用）。

vocabulary.definition: a thick piece of a tree trunk or branch — 原木；粗木段
collocations: a floating log 漂浮的木头
a hollow log 中空木段
a ship's log 航海日志
compare: log：一段粗木头
branch：树枝，不一定粗或已截断
snag：本文为卡在水底、危及船只的枯木
timber：木材的统称
vocabulary.usage: 本文 floating log 是漂浮木头，和后面嵌在河床的 snag 不同。log 作动词双写 g：logged、logging。

vocabulary.definition: easy to notice because it stands out — 显眼的；引人注目的
collocations: be conspicuous against a background 在背景衬托下显眼
a conspicuous feature 明显特征
conspicuous by one's absence 因本应出现却缺席而引人注意
compare: conspicuous：容易被看到，常因与周围反差大
obvious：容易被理解或判断
prominent：突出或重要，也可指视觉显著
inconspicuous：不显眼
vocabulary.usage: black and conspicuous 是描写漂浮木头的补充形容词；木头在金色水面上形成反差，未必有贬义。

vocabulary.partOfSpeech: v. [T]；本文在复合 adj. 中
vocabulary.definition: to add or give a shade of colour — 染色；使带某种色调
collocations: tinted glass 有色玻璃
a blue tint 淡蓝色调
many-tinted water 色彩斑斓的水面（本文）
compare: tint：一层或一种色调
hue：颜色类别或色相
shade：同一颜色的深浅变化
tinge：少量颜色，也常比喻感情的一丝
vocabulary.usage: many-tinted 是“有多种色调的”复合修饰语；as many-tinted as 是 as + 形容词 + as，不是 as many + 复数名词 + as 的数量比较。

vocabulary.definition: a gemstone often showing changing colours as it is viewed — 欧泊；蛋白石
collocations: an opal ring 欧泊戒指
an opal gemstone 欧泊宝石
the colours of an opal 欧泊的变彩
compare: opal：本文借其变幻色彩写水面
pearl：珍珠，来自贝类，不是同种材料
jade：玉，不能按中文“宝石”一概互换
vocabulary.usage: an opal 中用 an。本文 as an opal 是明喻，比较的是多彩光泽，不是河中真有欧泊。

vocabulary.definition: red or reddish, often with a warm tone — 红润的；泛红的
collocations: ruddy cheeks 红润的脸颊
a ruddy glow 红色光辉
a ruddy complexion 红润肤色
compare: ruddy：偏温暖、红润的红色
red：红色的广称
rosy：常写粉红、健康，也可比喻乐观
flushed：因热、情绪等而涨红
vocabulary.usage: ruddy flush 是霞光映在水面的红晕，不说明水面生病。也不在这里使用英式口语粗话替代义。
otherSenses: 英式较旧口语中可代 bloody 表恼怒、加强语气

vocabulary.definition: a large branch of a tree — 粗树枝；大枝
collocations: a leafy bough 枝叶茂盛的大枝
a low bough 低垂的大枝
a single living bough 唯一还活着的大枝
compare: bough：较粗大的枝，文学感强
branch：树枝的一般称呼，也能指分支机构
twig：细小末梢枝条
vocabulary.usage: 读 /baʊ/，不按 though 或 rough 的 -ough 来读。a single leafy bough 与整体 dead tree 的反差突出树仅余一枝的生命力。

vocabulary.definition: not blocked from view, movement or access — 无遮挡的；畅通的
collocations: an unobstructed view 毫无遮挡的视野
unobstructed access 无阻碍的通行
an unobstructed path 畅通的道路
compare: unobstructed：没有东西挡住
clear：清晰、晴朗或无障碍，范围广
unrestricted：没有人为限制
uninterrupted：过程不中断
vocabulary.usage: 本文修饰 splendor，指阳光无遮无挡地照过来，不是说光本身“没有规定”。un- 是否定前缀，中心来自 obstruct。
otherSenses: 行动或获得信息等不受阻碍的：unobstructed access

vocabulary.definition: impressive beauty or brilliance — 壮丽；辉煌；本文为灿烂光辉
collocations: in all its splendor 尽显壮美
the splendor of the sunset 落日的灿烂
restore something to its former splendor 恢复昔日辉煌
compare: splendor：壮美、华丽或光彩引人赞叹
beauty：美的一般概念
glow：柔和发光的视觉效果
grandeur：规模与气势宏伟
family: splendid adj. 极好的；壮丽的
vocabulary.usage: 英式 splendour；本文美式 splendor 保留。这里说太阳流泻的光辉；复数 splendors 可指各种美景。
otherSenses: splendors（复数）某地的壮美景物或特征

vocabulary.definition: to fascinate someone as if by magic — 使着迷；使如中魔法般陶醉
collocations: be bewitched by beauty 为美所迷
a bewitching scene 迷人景象
bewitch an audience 让观众着迷
compare: bewitch：像魔法般控制心神，修辞感强
fascinate：强烈吸引兴趣
charm：以可爱、亲切或美打动
enchant：使陶醉，也可有魔法义
vocabulary.usage: like one bewitched 指“像一个中了魔法的人”；bewitched 是后置分词，one 指人，不是数字一。
otherSenses: 给人施魔法或下咒（故事、文学语境）

vocabulary.definition: something splendid or beautiful that gives great pleasure — 壮丽景象；绚丽之美
collocations: the glories of nature 大自然的壮美
in all its glory 尽显风采
former glory 昔日的辉煌
compare: glory：令人赞叹的美或荣光
honour：声誉、尊敬与道德荣誉
beauty：广义的美
splendor：华丽壮美的气象
family: glorious adj. 光荣的；壮丽的
vocabulary.usage: 本文 glories 与 charms 并列，是景致之美，不是太阳获得了功勋。荣誉抽象义常不可数，美景可用复数。

vocabulary.definition: the dim light near the end of the day — 暮光；薄暮
collocations: at twilight 在薄暮时
in the twilight 在暮色中
the twilight of one's career 职业生涯末期
compare: twilight：天将黑时的微光与时段
sunset：太阳落到地平线下的过程
dusk：入夜前天色渐暗的时段
night：已经黑下来的夜间
vocabulary.usage: 本文与 moon、sun 并列成为 wrought 的施事，指暮色带来的光影；不能当作明确的钟点。
otherSenses: 文学比喻末期、衰退阶段：one's twilight years 晚年

vocabulary.definition: brought about or produced — 造成；创造出
collocations: changes wrought by something 某事带来的变化
wrought upon the river's face 在河面上造就（本文）
finely wrought 精心制作的
compare: wrought：本文为文学性的 produced/created
worked：现代 work 的常规过去式
wreaked：wreak 的规则过去式，常指造成破坏，不宜当全部 wrought 的唯一来源
family: work v. 工作；产生作用
vocabulary.usage: which … wrought … 中 wrought 是限定过去时谓语，宾语由 which 对应 glories and charms。Oxford 明确指出它是 work 的旧形式；不把这里解释成现在分词或普通形容词。

sources.label: Oxford · wrought（work 的旧式过去形式）
Cambridge · wrought（形容词及现代用法对照）

otherSenses: 现代一般工作经历用 worked

vocabulary.definition: rising steeply with a broad front — 陡直的；坡面突然升起的
collocations: bluff banks 陡直河岸
a bluff reef 陡直的水下沙脊（本文）
a bluff manner 直率的态度
compare: bluff：本文说水下坡面陡直
steep：陡的常用词
sheer：接近垂直
shallow：水浅，关注深度而非侧坡
family: bluff n. 陡岸；虚张声势
bluff adj. 陡直的；直率的
vocabulary.usage: 原书第 9 章前文解释 bluff reef 下方为侧面近乎直立的 sand-bar，不能机械译成珊瑚礁或“骗人的礁石”。Cambridge 常用义外，地形义补查 Merriam-Webster。
otherSenses: adj. 直率甚至略显粗鲁的

vocabulary.definition: a ridge of rock, coral or sand near the water's surface — 礁或水下隆起的脊；本文为危险的水下沙脊
collocations: a coral reef 珊瑚礁
a submerged reef 水下礁脊
a bluff reef 陡直沙脊（本文）
compare: reef：贴近水面的连续岩、珊瑚或沙脊
bar：常指水道内的沙洲
snag：卡在河床的枯木
rock：单块岩石，不一定形成长脊
vocabulary.usage: 不要把现代常见 coral reef 套到密西西比河。原书前文明确把此处 bluff reef 与陡直 sand-bar 联系起来，译为陡直沙脊更准确。
otherSenses: 此义可识别，无须当本篇核心动作背

vocabulary.definition: a submerged or partly submerged bank of sediment — 水下或半露水面的沙洲
collocations: a sand bar 沙洲
a bar in the river 河中的沙洲
cross a bar 越过沙洲水域
compare: bar：沉积形成、可能挡住航道的沙洲
reef：岩、沙或珊瑚形成的近水面脊
bank：岸或浅滩，范围较广
vocabulary.usage: a dissolving bar 是正在被水流冲蚀、改变的沙洲，不是酒吧关门，也不是盐溶于水那种化学过程。本文义补查 Merriam-Webster。
otherSenses: v. 禁止：bar someone from doing

vocabulary.definition: smooth and shiny, sometimes slippery — 光滑的；本文为平滑如镜的水面
collocations: slick water 平滑的水面
a slick surface 湿滑表面
a slick presentation 流畅娴熟的展示
compare: slick：平滑发亮，或做得娴熟却可能油滑
smooth：表面平滑或过程顺畅，较中性
slippery：容易滑倒，强调摩擦小
calm：水面平静，不一定带光泽
family: slick v. 使光滑（常用 slick back）
slick adj. 光滑的；娴熟的
vocabulary.usage: 本文仅描述水面形态，不能因此推断有石油污染。oil slick 的 slick 为名词，和此处形容词不同。
otherSenses: adj. 表演、制作娴熟流畅的
v. 把头发抹平向后梳

vocabulary.definition: in the place over there — 在那边；远处
collocations: over yonder 在那边（旧式）
yonder hill 那边的山（文学）
the town yonder 那边的城镇
compare: yonder：旧式或地域性的“那边”
there：一般的在那里
over there：现代常用的指示远处表达
beyond：超过某个界限的另一边
vocabulary.usage: 现代主动表达通常用 over there。本文 over yonder 指说话人示意的远处，不是正式精确方位，也不是 beyond 的同义替换。
otherSenses: 也作限定词，修饰那边的人或物

vocabulary.definition: to become shallower — 变浅；淤浅
collocations: the channel is shoaling 航道在变浅
shoal up 淤浅（本文）
a shoal of fish 一群鱼
compare: shoal（v.）：水深逐渐减小
silt up：泥沙淤积堵塞，强调原因
dry up：水消失或干涸
deepen：变深，与 shoal 相反
vocabulary.usage: is shoaling up 是现在进行时，不能译成“鱼在聚集”。Cambridge 给出浅滩等名词义，本文动词义补查 Merriam-Webster。
otherSenses: v. 鱼等聚群（另一语境）

vocabulary.definition: a long narrow mark contrasting with its surroundings — 条纹；细长痕迹
collocations: a silver streak 一道银色纹痕
a streak of light 一道光
a streak of grey 灰白的一缕
compare: streak：狭长、与背景对比明显的痕
stripe：较规则的带状条纹
trail：运动后留下的一路痕迹
line：线条的泛称
family: streak v. 飞驰；使带条纹
vocabulary.usage: 本文是阴影中的一道银色水纹，后文解释其航行含义。不要用比赛的 winning streak 义理解。
otherSenses: 性格中某种特质：a stubborn streak

vocabulary.definition: a tree or branch lodged in a riverbed and dangerous to boats — 嵌在河床、威胁航行的枯木
collocations: a submerged snag 水下枯木
hit a snag 遇到障碍
snag a sleeve on a nail 袖子被钉子钩破
compare: snag：本文为固定在水底的危险木头
log：粗木段，原文可自由漂浮
reef：沙、岩等形成的水下脊
obstacle：障碍的泛称
vocabulary.usage: 本文随后用 he、himself、fish for steamboats 将 snag 拟人化，说它像在“钓”船。不能只译成抽象“小麻烦”；航行义补查 Merriam-Webster。

vocabulary.definition: a sense of excitement, mystery and imaginative appeal — 浪漫情趣；诗意的吸引力
collocations: the romance of travel 旅行的浪漫
lose its romance 失去浪漫色彩
a historical romance 历史爱情小说
compare: romance：让想象活跃的情趣或神秘吸引力
love：对人或事的爱
beauty：美的性质或体验
nostalgia：对往昔的怀念
vocabulary.usage: 本文不是说作者与大河谈恋爱，而是专业习惯使惊叹与诗意退去。这个义通常不可数；两种名词重音均有词典依据。
otherSenses: n. [U] 恋爱中的浪漫情调

vocabulary.definition: to bring about or achieve something — 达到；实现
collocations: compass an end 达到目的（旧式）
compassing safe piloting 实现安全领航（本文）
a magnetic compass 磁罗盘
compare: compass（v.）：这里相当于 achieve/accomplish，旧式
navigate：实际导航或穿行
encompass：包含、环绕
compass（n.）：指南针，不是此处词性
family: compass v. 实现；环绕（旧式）
vocabulary.usage: toward 是介词，所以后用 compassing；它不是“使用指南针”的普通动词说法。本文动词义补查 Merriam-Webster；现代笔记可释 achieve。
otherSenses: compasses/a pair of compasses 圆规

vocabulary.definition: gradual damage, deterioration or breakdown — 衰败；腐坏；本文为隐藏的身体病变
collocations: signs of decay 衰败迹象
tooth decay 蛀牙
fall into decay 逐渐破败
compare: decay：逐步坏损或分解
decline：水平、数量或状态下降
rot：生物性腐烂，具体感强
disease：疾病，不等同所有衰变
vocabulary.usage: 本文 hidden decay 是医生类比中隐藏的病变，不是评论人物道德腐败。名词、动词同读音同重音；decay 一般不用复数表示过程。
otherSenses: 名词也可指建筑、制度或道德的衰败

vocabulary.definition: unhealthy or harmful to well-being — 不健康的；有害的
collocations: an unwholesome condition 不健康的状态
unwholesome food 不健康的食物
an unwholesome influence 不良影响
compare: unwholesome：不利于身体、心理或道德健康
unhealthy：健康不佳或有损健康，较常用
immoral：违反道德标准，不是本文义
unpleasant：令人不快，不一定有害
vocabulary.usage: 本文 her unwholesome condition 指医生眼中的身体状况，不要误译为女性品行不端。整段是文学类比和反问，未断言所有医生都丧失审美能力。
otherSenses: 也可形容环境、内容或影响在精神、道德层面不良

sentences.text: From a child I was fond of reading, and all the little money that came into my hands was ever laid out in books.
sentences.translation: 我从小就爱读书，到手的所有那点钱总是花在书上。

classification.label: 并列复合句
classification.reason: 同时包含主句之间的并列以及内部或附加的限定从句。
classification.note: 两套主干由 and 连接；第二套内含修饰 money 的定语从句。little 是钱少，不是小孩子的钱；ever 在旧语境表示总是。from a child 可现代改写为 from childhood。

clauses: all the little money … was ever laid out in books
that came into my hands 修饰 money
sentences.note: 两套主干由 and 连接；第二套内含修饰 money 的定语从句。little 是钱少，不是小孩子的钱；ever 在旧语境表示总是。from a child 可现代改写为 from childhood。
sentences.paraphrase: I loved reading from childhood and spent every little sum I received on books.

reuse.zh: 我收到的所有钱都存了起来。
reuse.en: All the money that I received was saved.
reuse.note: money 作不可数主语，谓语用 was；that 引出定语从句。

pdfNotes.title: 从读书经历看自我教育
pdfNotes.text: 封面与导图把富兰克林呈现为热爱阅读、主动学习的人。本文的重点是他怎样利用有限的书、学徒生活和写作练习培养自己；传记成就作为背景，不代替原文的具体证据。

pdfNotes.title: lay out 与 lay / lie
pdfNotes.text: lay out 在此是把钱花在书上；现代常说 lay out money on something。原文 all the little money 强调钱虽少却全花了，并非花费总额很大。lay—laid—laid；lie“躺”是 lie—lay—lain，lie“撒谎”是 lie—lied—lied。

sentences.text: Pleased with The Pilgrim's Progress, I began collecting John Bunyan's works in separate little volumes.
sentences.translation: 我很喜欢《天路历程》，最初收藏的是约翰·班扬作品的分册小本。

classification.label: 简单句
classification.reason: 一个展开的限定主句；共用主语的并列谓语、非谓语或缩略表达另作提示。
classification.note: 这是带悬垂分词的旧式松散表达，不能说 collection 感到高兴。现代可改 Pleased with the book, I began collecting Bunyan's works。原文 the The 重复，保留音频对应原句并在此指出，不当正确拼写来背。

clauses: I began collecting John Bunyan’s works …
Pleased with The Pilgrim’s Progress 修饰 I
sentences.note: 删除书名前重复的 the，并改写悬垂分词：Pleased with 的语义主体为 I。
sentences.paraphrase: Because I enjoyed The Pilgrim's Progress, I began by collecting small editions of Bunyan's works.

reuse.zh: 对结果很满意，我决定继续这项练习。
reuse.en: Pleased with the result, I decided to continue the exercise.
reuse.note: 分词的感受者与主句 I 一致，修正原句悬垂结构后再迁移。

pdfNotes.title: Pleased 的逻辑主体与书名重复
pdfNotes.text: Pleased with… 表达“我”读书后的感受，但形式主语是 my first collection，存在逻辑主体不一致的宽松接续。正式仿写可改成 Pleased with the book, I began collecting…，不要让 collection 成为感到高兴的人。网页与 PDF 的 the The 重复属于文本问题，书名 The Pilgrim's Progress 前无需再加 the。

pdfNotes.title: volume 与 separate 的含义
pdfNotes.text: separate little volumes 是分开成册的小开本书，不是每本书各自形成一套丛书。volume 在此是“册／卷”，还常指音量、体积或总量；不要用 everyday 的“音量”义解释藏书。

sentences.text: I afterward sold them to enable me to buy R. Burton's Historical Collections; they were small chapmen's books, and cheap, 40 or 50 in all.
sentences.translation: 后来我把这些书卖掉，用钱买了 R. Burton 的《历史汇编》；那些书是小贩兜售的小册子，便宜，总共四五十本。

classification.label: 并列句
classification.reason: 两个或以上并列主句，各自具有主语与限定谓语。
classification.note: 分号连接两个主句；cheap 与名词短语共同说明 they，并未另起主句。enable me to buy 是使役式宾语加不定式，them 回指先前的藏书，they 指新买的那套小册子。

clauses: they were small chapmen's books, and cheap
functions: to enable me to buy R. Burton's Historical Collections;
sentences.note: 分号连接两个主句；cheap 与名词短语共同说明 they，并未另起主句。enable me to buy 是使役式宾语加不定式，them 回指先前的藏书，they 指新买的那套小册子。
sentences.paraphrase: I later sold those books to buy Burton's inexpensive historical booklets, about forty or fifty in all.

reuse.zh: 我借给她一本词典，好让她查这些词。
reuse.en: I lent her a dictionary to enable her to look up these words.
reuse.note: to enable 表目的；enable + 宾语 + to do。

pdfNotes.title: chapmen 是商贩，不是人名
pdfNotes.text: chapman 是“行商、货郎”的旧词，复数 chapmen；chapmen's books 指由商贩售卖的廉价小册子。不要因为讲义提到 George Chapman 就把此处当成作家姓氏。40 or 50 in all 说明总数量，并不说明书有四五十页。

sentences.text: My father's little library consisted chiefly of books in polemic divinity, most of which I read, and have since often regretted that, at a time when I had such a thirst for knowledge, more proper books had not fallen in my way since it was now resolved I should not be a clergyman.
sentences.translation: 父亲的小书库主要是论辩神学的书，大多数我都读过；后来我常后悔，在我如此渴求知识时竟没遇上更合适的书，因为当时已决定不让我做神职人员。

classification.label: 并列复合句
classification.reason: 同时包含主句之间的并列以及内部或附加的限定从句。
classification.note: and have regretted 语义主语是 I，不能接到 library 上；这是旧文的松散衔接，现代宜补 I。regretted 的内容先插入时间，再到 books had not fallen；最后 since 是因为，resolved 后省略 that，决定者未明确写出。

clauses: My father's little library consisted chiefly of books …
most of which I read 修饰 books
that … more proper books had not fallen in my way
when I had such a thirst … 修饰 a time
(that) I should not be a clergyman
functions: when I had such a thirst for knowledge,
I should not be a clergyman.
sentences.note: and have regretted 语义主语是 I，不能接到 library 上；这是旧文的松散衔接，现代宜补 I。regretted 的内容先插入时间，再到 books had not fallen；最后 since 是因为，resolved 后省略 that，决定者未明确写出。
sentences.paraphrase: My father's books were mainly religious controversies. I read most of them, but later regretted lacking better reading when I was eager to learn and was no longer expected to enter the clergy.

reuse.pattern: I regret that, at a time when ___, ___.
reuse.zh: 我遗憾的是，在大家需要帮助的时候，我不在场。
reuse.en: I regret that, at a time when everyone needed help, I was absent.
reuse.note: that 内容从句中插入带 when 定语从句的时间状语。

pdfNotes.title: 谁在 regret，谁作了决定
pdfNotes.text: have since often regretted 的行为者是 I，不是 library；旧文的连接较松散，现代改写宜明确补出 and I…。regretted 后接 that 内容从句，when 修饰 time，since 引出原因。it was resolved 没有明说决定者，不应擅自改成“我自己决定不当牧师”。

pdfNotes.title: divinity 与渴望知识
pdfNotes.text: polemic divinity 在此指宗教论争／神学辩论；divinity 的语境义是“神学”，不是神性。a thirst for knowledge 是求知欲；thirst 在这里是比喻，不能据此判断一个人真的口渴。

sentences.text: Plutarch's Lives there was in which I read abundantly, and I still think that time spent to great advantage.
sentences.translation: 书库里还有《普鲁塔克名人传》，我读了很多，至今仍认为那段时间花得很有价值。

classification.label: 并列复合句
classification.reason: 同时包含主句之间的并列以及内部或附加的限定从句。
classification.note: 书名虽以 Lives 结尾，但指一部作品，用 was。第二部分 that 是限定词“那段”，that time 是 think 的宾语，spent… 为过去分词宾补，不把 that 标作宾语从句引导词。

clauses: there was Plutarch's Lives（书名提到句首）
I still think that time spent to great advantage
sentences.note: 书名虽以 Lives 结尾，但指一部作品，用 was。第二部分 that 是限定词“那段”，that time 是 think 的宾语，spent… 为过去分词宾补，不把 that 标作宾语从句引导词。
sentences.paraphrase: There was a copy of Plutarch's Lives, which I read extensively; I still regard that reading time as well spent.

reuse.zh: 我认为花在阅读上的时间花得很值。
reuse.en: I consider the time I spend reading well spent.
reuse.note: consider + 宾语 + 过去分词补足语；well spent 描述 time。

pdfNotes.title: 书名提前，think 后接宾语补足语
pdfNotes.text: Plutarch's Lives there was 是把书名提前突出，正常语序可理解为 There was Plutarch's Lives…。书名虽含 Lives，整体指一部作品，was 不由单词外形决定。think that time spent… 中 that time 是宾语，spent… 是过去分词补足语，不能把 that 当成从句连词。

sentences.text: There was also a book of Defoe's, called An Essay on Projects, and another of Dr. Mather's, called Essays to Do Good, which perhaps gave me a turn of thinking that had an influence on some of the principal future events of my life.
sentences.translation: 还有笛福的一本《论计划》，以及马瑟博士的《行善论》；后一本也许使我形成了一种思考倾向，影响了我后来人生中的一些大事。

classification.label: 主从复合句
classification.reason: 主句带有限定从句；按主干、从属关系和内部成分逐层拆解。
classification.note: two called 短语只命名书，不是独立限定从句。which 按邻近关系与后文思想影响指向 Mather 的书，perhaps 保留推测；a book of Defoe's 是双重属格。

clauses: There was also a book of Defoe's … and another of Dr. Mather's
called An Essay on Projects／called Essays to Do Good
which perhaps gave me a turn of thinking …
that had an influence … 修饰 a turn of thinking
functions: which perhaps gave me a turn of thinking
that had an influence on some of the principal future events of my life.
sentences.note: two called 短语只命名书，不是独立限定从句。which 按邻近关系与后文思想影响指向 Mather 的书，perhaps 保留推测；a book of Defoe's 是双重属格。
sentences.paraphrase: Books by Defoe and Mather were also available; Mather's may have helped shape a way of thinking that influenced important events in my later life.

reuse.zh: 那里有一本叫《小王子》的书，它鼓励我换个角度思考。
reuse.en: There was a book, called The Little Prince, which encouraged me to think differently.
reuse.note: called 为命名用的分词定语；which 为限定谓语从句的主语。

pdfNotes.title: a turn of thinking 是思维取向
pdfNotes.text: turn 在这里侧重思维的倾向、取向，不必理解成一次突然的转变。perhaps 给书籍对人生的影响保留了推测语气；准确改写应保留这种不确定性，不把“或许影响了”改成毫无保留的事实断言。

sentences.text: This bookish inclination at length determined my father to make me a printer, though he had already one son (James) of that profession.
sentences.translation: 这种爱书的倾向终于使父亲决定让我当印刷工，尽管他已有一个儿子詹姆斯从事这一行。

classification.label: 主从复合句
classification.reason: 主句带有限定从句；按主干、从属关系和内部成分逐层拆解。
classification.note: determine somebody to do 是促使某人作决定的旧用法。to make me a printer 内 me 是宾语、a printer 是宾补。though 后的 had 为实义动词“有”，不是过去完成时助动词。

clauses: This bookish inclination … determined my father to make me a printer
though he had already one son … of that profession
functions: though he had already one son (James) of that profession.
sentences.note: determine somebody to do 是促使某人作决定的旧用法。to make me a printer 内 me 是宾语、a printer 是宾补。though 后的 had 为实义动词“有”，不是过去完成时助动词。
sentences.paraphrase: My love of books eventually led my father to choose printing for me, although my brother James already worked in that trade.

reuse.zh: 这次谈话让我重新考虑，尽管我已经做了决定。
reuse.en: The conversation led me to reconsider, though I had already made a decision.
reuse.note: 用现代 lead somebody to do 迁移原句的旧式 determine somebody to do。

pdfNotes.title: determine somebody to do 的旧式用法
pdfNotes.text: This bookish inclination 是促使父亲作决定的原因；determine somebody to do 是较旧式、正式的用法，现代可改为 lead somebody to decide to do。at length 此处是“终于”，不要混入后文“详细地”的意思。

sentences.text: In 1717 my brother James returned from England with a press and letters to set up his business in Boston.
sentences.translation: 1717 年，哥哥詹姆斯从英国带着印刷机和活字回来，在波士顿开办印刷业务。

classification.label: 简单句
classification.reason: 一个展开的限定主句；共用主语的并列谓语、非谓语或缩略表达另作提示。
classification.note: James 是 brother 的同位语；with 表示携带。letters 与 press 同属印刷设备，是活字；to set up 的逻辑主语为 James。只有 returned 为限定谓语。

clauses: my brother James returned from England …
to set up his business in Boston
functions: to set up his business in Boston.
sentences.note: James 是 brother 的同位语；with 表示携带。letters 与 press 同属印刷设备，是活字；to set up 的逻辑主语为 James。只有 returned 为限定谓语。
sentences.paraphrase: In 1717 James brought a printing press and movable type back from England to start a business in Boston.

reuse.zh: 她带着新笔记从图书馆回来，准备修改文章。
reuse.en: She returned from the library with new notes to revise her essay.
reuse.note: with 为携带；to revise 为目的。

pdfNotes.title: press and letters 是印刷设备
pdfNotes.text: press 是印刷机；与之并列的 letters 是印刷用的活字，结合 set up his business 理解。这里没有授权机构或文件的证据，不把 letters 加译成许可证或相关证书；movable type 是清楚的现代改写。

sentences.text: I liked it much better than that of my father, but still had a hankering for the sea.
sentences.translation: 我喜欢这一行，远胜父亲的那一行，但仍向往海上生活。

classification.label: 简单句
classification.reason: 一个展开的限定主句；共用主语的并列谓语、非谓语或缩略表达另作提示。
classification.note: liked 与 had 共用 I，按一个主句的并列谓语处理。it 是印刷职业，that 替代职业以免重复；the sea 借指航海生活，不是比较谁更喜欢大海。

clauses: I liked it … but still had a hankering for the sea
much better than that of my father
functions: much better than that of my father,
sentences.note: liked 与 had 共用 I，按一个主句的并列谓语处理。it 是印刷职业，that 替代职业以免重复；the sea 借指航海生活，不是比较谁更喜欢大海。
sentences.paraphrase: I preferred printing to my father's trade, but I still wanted a life at sea.

reuse.pattern: I liked ___ better than ___, but still ___.
reuse.zh: 我更喜欢这份草稿而非上一份，但仍想修改结尾。
reuse.en: I liked this draft better than the previous one, but still wanted to revise the ending.
reuse.note: but 后 wanted 与 liked 共享主语 I。

pdfNotes.title: 预想的后果与学徒契约
pdfNotes.text: apprehended effect 指父亲担心发生的后果，不是“被逮捕的结果”。have me bound to my brother 中 me 是宾语，bound… 是过去分词补足语，表示安排我按契约跟哥哥学艺；不能把这里的 be bound to 与“肯定会做”的另一结构混同。

sentences.text: To prevent the apprehended effect of such an inclination, my father was impatient to have me bound to my brother.
sentences.translation: 为防止这种倾向带来他所担心的后果，父亲急着要我与哥哥订立学徒契约。

classification.label: 简单句
classification.reason: 一个展开的限定主句；共用主语的并列谓语、非谓语或缩略表达另作提示。
classification.note: to have… 补足 impatient；内部 have + me + bound… 表示安排我受契约约束。apprehended 是修饰 effect 的分词，并非另一个谓语；担忧来自父亲。

clauses: my father was impatient to have me bound to my brother
functions: To prevent the apprehended effect of such an inclination,
to have me bound to my brother.
sentences.note: to have… 补足 impatient；内部 have + me + bound… 表示安排我受契约约束。apprehended 是修饰 effect 的分词，并非另一个谓语；担忧来自父亲。
sentences.paraphrase: Fearing that I might go to sea, my father was eager to arrange my apprenticeship with James.

reuse.zh: 为防止出错，我们请人检查了所有数字。
reuse.en: To prevent errors, we had all the figures checked.
reuse.note: have + 宾语 + 过去分词，数字是被检查的对象。

pdfNotes.title: 预想的后果与学徒契约
pdfNotes.text: apprehended effect 指父亲担心发生的后果，不是“被逮捕的结果”。have me bound to my brother 中 me 是宾语，bound… 是过去分词补足语，表示安排我按契约跟哥哥学艺；不能把这里的 be bound to 与“肯定会做”的另一结构混同。

sentences.text: I stood out some time, but at last was persuaded, and signed the indentures when I was yet but twelve years old.
sentences.translation: 我起初坚持了一阵，最后还是被说服了，才十二岁就签了学徒契约。

classification.label: 主从复合句
classification.reason: 主句带有限定从句；按主干、从属关系和内部成分逐层拆解。
classification.note: 三个谓语共享 I；when 使全句含限定从句。stood out 在旧文是坚持不答应，yet but 相当于当时才；不是 still not。

clauses: I stood out … but … was persuaded, and signed the indentures
when I was yet but twelve years old
functions: when I was yet but twelve years old.
sentences.note: 三个谓语共享 I；when 使全句含限定从句。stood out 在旧文是坚持不答应，yet but 相当于当时才；不是 still not。
sentences.paraphrase: I resisted for a while, but eventually agreed and signed the apprenticeship contract at only twelve.

reuse.zh: 我起初犹豫，但听完解释后最终同意了。
reuse.en: I hesitated, but eventually agreed when I heard the explanation.
reuse.note: 主句谓语共享 I；when 引出完整时间从句。

pdfNotes.title: stand out、yet but 与 only
pdfNotes.text: stood out 是暂不答应的旧义；yet but twelve 是当时才十二岁，but 相当于 only。第 12 句 only 引出例外，相当于 except that／不过，并非只修饰紧随其后的 I。be to do 表示当时约定的安排。

sentences.text: I was to serve as an apprentice till I was twenty-one years of age, only I was to be allowed journeyman's wages during the last year.
sentences.translation: 按约我须当学徒直到二十一岁，不过最后一年可以领熟练工的工资。

classification.label: 并列复合句
classification.reason: 同时包含主句之间的并列以及内部或附加的限定从句。
classification.note: only 在此引出例外，相当于 except that；两个主句都有 I，第一主句内还有 till 时间从句，因此是并列复合句。be to do 表示契约安排，并非主观愿望。

clauses: I was to serve as an apprentice …
till I was twenty-one years of age
only I was to be allowed journeyman's wages …
functions: till I was twenty-one years of age,
sentences.note: only 在此引出例外，相当于 except that；两个主句都有 I，第一主句内还有 till 时间从句，因此是并列复合句。be to do 表示契约安排，并非主观愿望。
sentences.paraphrase: The contract required me to remain an apprentice until twenty-one, with skilled-worker pay only in the final year.

reuse.pattern: I was to ___ until ___, except that ___.
reuse.zh: 我原定工作到六月，不过最后一周可以请假。
reuse.en: I was to work until June, except that I could take the final week off.
reuse.note: was to 表原定安排；用 except that 清晰表达原句 only 的例外义。

pdfNotes.title: stand out、yet but 与 only
pdfNotes.text: stood out 是暂不答应的旧义；yet but twelve 是当时才十二岁，but 相当于 only。第 12 句 only 引出例外，相当于 except that／不过，并非只修饰紧随其后的 I。be to do 表示当时约定的安排。

sentences.text: In a little time I made great proficiency in the business, and became a useful hand to my brother.
sentences.translation: 不久我在这一行就熟练多了，成了哥哥的得力帮手。

classification.label: 简单句
classification.reason: 一个展开的限定主句；共用主语的并列谓语、非谓语或缩略表达另作提示。
classification.note: made 与 became 共用 I。great proficiency 在原文是技能进步，现代可写 made great progress；a useful hand 借指能干的工人。

clauses: I made great proficiency … and became a useful hand …
sentences.note: made 与 became 共用 I。great proficiency 在原文是技能进步，现代可写 made great progress；a useful hand 借指能干的工人。
sentences.paraphrase: I soon developed skill in printing and became a capable assistant to my brother.

reuse.zh: 不久，她就成了团队的得力助手。
reuse.en: In a short time, she became a valuable assistant to the team.
reuse.note: became 是系动词，后接表语。

pdfNotes.title: 手艺、人手与借书关系
pdfNotes.text: a useful hand 把人手借指能干的工人；proficiency 是熟练程度，原文 made great proficiency 可现代改写为 made great progress。an acquaintance with… 在这里是与书商学徒的相识关系，不是“某个熟人”；one 代一本小书。

sentences.text: I now had access to better books.
sentences.translation: 现在我能接触到更好的书了。

classification.label: 简单句
classification.reason: 一个展开的限定主句；共用主语的并列谓语、非谓语或缩略表达另作提示。
classification.note: have access to 是有机会接触或使用；to 是介词，后接 books。比较级 better 隐含与先前可得到的书相比。

clauses: I now had access to better books
sentences.note: have access to 是有机会接触或使用；to 是介词，后接 books。比较级 better 隐含与先前可得到的书相比。
sentences.paraphrase: I could now obtain better books.

reuse.zh: 每个学生都能使用学校图书馆。
reuse.en: Every student had access to the school library.
reuse.note: access to 中 to 是介词。

pdfNotes.title: 手艺、人手与借书关系
pdfNotes.text: a useful hand 把人手借指能干的工人；proficiency 是熟练程度，原文 made great proficiency 可现代改写为 made great progress。an acquaintance with… 在这里是与书商学徒的相识关系，不是“某个熟人”；one 代一本小书。

sentences.text: An acquaintance with the apprentices of booksellers enabled me sometimes to borrow a small one, which I was careful to return soon and clean.
sentences.translation: 因为结识了一些书商的学徒，我有时能借到一本小书，总是小心地尽快、干净地归还。

classification.label: 主从复合句
classification.reason: 主句带有限定从句；按主干、从属关系和内部成分逐层拆解。
classification.note: which 是 return 的宾语；clean 说明书归还时的状态，不是副词。主语 acquaintance 是相识关系；one 代一本小书，不指一个学徒。

clauses: An acquaintance … enabled me … to borrow a small one
which I was careful to return soon and clean
functions: An acquaintance with the apprentices of booksellers
sentences.note: which 是 return 的宾语；clean 说明书归还时的状态，不是副词。主语 acquaintance 是相识关系；one 代一本小书，不指一个学徒。
sentences.paraphrase: Knowing booksellers' apprentices sometimes let me borrow a small book, which I took care to return promptly and clean.

reuse.zh: 奖学金使我能够买一台电脑，我每天都使用它。
reuse.en: The scholarship enabled me to buy a computer, which I used every day.
reuse.note: which 回指 computer，在从句中作 used 的宾语。

pdfNotes.title: 手艺、人手与借书关系
pdfNotes.text: a useful hand 把人手借指能干的工人；proficiency 是熟练程度，原文 made great proficiency 可现代改写为 made great progress。an acquaintance with… 在这里是与书商学徒的相识关系，不是“某个熟人”；one 代一本小书。

pdfNotes.title: clean、sat up 与 wanted
pdfNotes.text: return … clean 中 clean 是说明书归还时状态的形容词；soon 才是时间副词。sat up 是熬夜未睡。lest 从句说明担心书主发现书不在或需要用书；wanted 在这里是“被需要”，讲义改写 in need 会变成书自身缺乏什么，应改为 needed。

sentences.text: Often I sat up in my room reading the greatest part of the night, when the book was borrowed in the evening and to be returned early in the morning, lest it should be missed or wanted.
sentences.translation: 若傍晚借的书必须次日清早归还，我常在房里读到深夜，以免书主发现书不在，或要用时找不到。

classification.label: 主从复合句
classification.reason: 主句带有限定从句；按主干、从属关系和内部成分逐层拆解。
classification.note: when 说明那些借书须隔夜归还的情境；and 后省略 was。reading 是 I 的伴随行为；lest 含以免，missed 与 wanted 共用 be，wanted 指书被需要。

clauses: Often I sat up in my room reading …
when the book was borrowed … and (was) to be returned …
lest it should be missed or wanted
functions: reading the greatest part of the night,
when the book was borrowed in the evening and to be returned early in the morning,
lest it should be missed or wanted.
sentences.note: when 说明那些借书须隔夜归还的情境；and 后省略 was。reading 是 I 的伴随行为；lest 含以免，missed 与 wanted 共用 be，wanted 指书被需要。
sentences.paraphrase: When a book had to be returned early the next morning, I often stayed up reading so its owner would not miss or need it before I returned it.

reuse.zh: 我把地址写下来，以免自己忘记。
reuse.en: I wrote down the address lest I should forget it.
reuse.note: lest 已含以免，通常不再加 not；此句属正式表达。

pdfNotes.title: clean、sat up 与 wanted
pdfNotes.text: return … clean 中 clean 是说明书归还时状态的形容词；soon 才是时间副词。sat up 是熬夜未睡。lest 从句说明担心书主发现书不在或需要用书；wanted 在这里是“被需要”，讲义改写 in need 会变成书自身缺乏什么，应改为 needed。

sentences.text: And after some time an ingenious tradesman, Mr. Matthew Adams, who had a pretty collection of books, and who frequented our printing-house, took notice of me, invited me to his library, and very kindly lent me such books as I chose to read.
sentences.translation: 又过了一阵，心灵手巧的商人马修·亚当斯先生注意到了我；他藏书颇丰，又常来印刷所，于是邀我去他的藏书室，慷慨地把我选中的书借给我读。

classification.label: 主从复合句
classification.reason: 主句带有限定从句；按主干、从属关系和内部成分逐层拆解。
classification.note: 主干被两层人物说明拉长，先连起 tradesman—took／invited／lent。as 是关系词，在 read 后留下宾语位置；不把 such…as 当结果从句。

clauses: an ingenious tradesman … took notice of me, invited me … and lent me …
who had … and who frequented … 修饰 Adams
as I chose to read 修饰 such books
functions: who had a pretty collection of books,
sentences.note: 主干被两层人物说明拉长，先连起 tradesman—took／invited／lent。as 是关系词，在 read 后留下宾语位置；不把 such…as 当结果从句。
sentences.paraphrase: Matthew Adams, a resourceful tradesman who often visited our shop and had a good library, noticed me and kindly let me borrow the books I wanted.

reuse.zh: 陈女士经常来书店，她邀请我参加读书会。
reuse.en: Ms Chen, who often visited the bookshop, invited me to join a reading group.
reuse.note: who 从句补充人物信息；主干是 Ms Chen invited me。

pdfNotes.title: 两个 who 与 such … as
pdfNotes.text: 两个并列的 who 从句都修饰 Matthew Adams；主句谓语为 took notice、invited、lent。such books as I chose to read 中 as 在定语从句内作 read 的宾语，不能把它当作 such … that 结果结构。frequent 作动词指常去，重音在后：/frɪˈkwent/。

sentences.text: I now took a fancy to poetry, and made some little pieces; my brother, thinking it might turn to account, encouraged me, and put me on composing occasional ballads.
sentences.translation: 我开始喜欢诗歌，写了几篇小作；哥哥认为或许有利可图，便鼓励我，让我写些应景歌谣。

classification.label: 并列复合句
classification.reason: 同时包含主句之间的并列以及内部或附加的限定从句。
classification.note: 分号分开 I 与 my brother 两个主句；thinking 虽是非谓语，但其内容 it might… 是限定从句，因此全句为并列复合。occasional 在此是因特定事件而作。

clauses: I took a fancy to poetry, and made some little pieces
my brother … encouraged me, and put me on composing …
functions: thinking it might turn to account,
sentences.note: 分号分开 I 与 my brother 两个主句；thinking 虽是非谓语，但其内容 it might… 是限定从句，因此全句为并列复合。occasional 在此是因特定事件而作。
sentences.paraphrase: I began writing poetry, and my brother encouraged event-based ballads because he thought they might earn money.

reuse.zh: 老师认为这个想法值得一试，便鼓励我继续。
reuse.en: My teacher, thinking the idea was worth trying, encouraged me to continue.
reuse.note: thinking 的逻辑主语是 teacher；其后省略 that。

pdfNotes.title: 应景歌谣与旧式鼓励表达
pdfNotes.text: occasional ballads 是为特定事件而作的歌谣；不能只译为偶尔创作。it might turn to account 在此是不及物用法，指能派上用场、带来收益；put me on composing 是旧式“促使我开始写”，现代可用 encouraged me to compose。

sentences.text: One was called The Lighthouse Tragedy, and contained an account of the drowning of Captain Worthilake, with his two daughters; the other was a sailor's song, on the taking of Teach (or Blackbeard) the pirate.
sentences.translation: 一首叫《灯塔悲剧》，讲沃思莱克船长与两个女儿溺亡的事；另一首是水手之歌，唱的是海盗蒂奇（即黑胡子）被拿下的故事。

classification.label: 并列句
classification.reason: 两个或以上并列主句，各自具有主语与限定谓语。
classification.note: one…the other 对应两首歌，分号连两个主句；with two daughters 不是增加一个并列主语。原文家属身份与历史资料有差别，详见 Context 的核对说明。

clauses: One was called … and contained an account …
the other was a sailor's song …
functions: an account of the drowning of Captain Worthilake,
on the taking of Teach (or Blackbeard) the pirate.
sentences.note: one…the other 对应两首歌，分号连两个主句；with two daughters 不是增加一个并列主语。原文家属身份与历史资料有差别，详见 Context 的核对说明。
sentences.paraphrase: One ballad described the drowning as Franklin remembered it; the other concerned the defeat of the pirate Blackbeard.

reuse.zh: 一篇文章讨论阅读，另一篇讨论写作。
reuse.en: One article discusses reading; the other discusses writing.
reuse.note: one…the other 表已知两者；两边有各自主谓结构。

pdfNotes.title: 诗歌事件与回忆中的事实差别
pdfNotes.text: 讲义指出作者把灯塔守卫的妻女记成了两个女儿。美国国家公园管理局 Boston Light 资料确认遇难者包括守卫 George Worthylake、妻子 Anne 和女儿 Ruth。原句与原音频照录作者回忆；理解史实应把它与历史记录区分，不能反过来修改音频对应原句。

sentences.text: They were wretched stuff, in the Grub-street-ballad style; and when they were printed he sent me about the town to sell them.
sentences.translation: 这些都是蹩脚作品，属于格拉布街式的廉价歌谣；印好后，哥哥便派我在城里四处售卖。

classification.label: 并列复合句
classification.reason: 同时包含主句之间的并列以及内部或附加的限定从句。
classification.note: they 与 them 都指歌谣；he 是哥哥。to sell 的逻辑主语为被派去的 me；sent 不能误写作 set，about 是在城里四处。

clauses: he sent me about the town to sell them
sentences.note: they 与 them 都指歌谣；he 是哥哥。to sell 的逻辑主语为被派去的 me；sent 不能误写作 set，about 是在城里四处。
sentences.paraphrase: The ballads were poor commercial verse, and my brother sent me around town to sell them after printing.

reuse.zh: 材料准备好后，老师派我去领取。
reuse.en: When the materials were ready, the teacher sent me to collect them.
reuse.note: sent 为 send 的过去式，to collect 表被派去做的事。

pdfNotes.title: send somebody about the town
pdfNotes.text: 原句是 sent me about the town：派我到城里四处售卖。讲义写成 set somebody about somewhere，应改回 send；另一个 set somebody to work 才是让某人着手工作的现代表达。Grub Street 在这里指为谋生大量生产的廉价作品，是作者对早期诗作的自嘲。

sentences.text: The first sold wonderfully, the event being recent, having made a great noise.
sentences.translation: 第一首卖得极好，因为题材是新近发生、引起了很大轰动的事件。

classification.label: 简单句
classification.reason: 一个展开的限定主句；共用主语的并列谓语、非谓语或缩略表达另作提示。
classification.note: sold 为不及物主动形式，说明销路。独立结构的主语 event 不等于主句 The first，两个分词补充该事件的新近性和影响；没有额外限定从句，但值得重点讲解。

clauses: the event being recent, having made a great noise
sentences.note: sold 为不及物主动形式，说明销路。独立结构的主语 event 不等于主句 The first，两个分词补充该事件的新近性和影响；没有额外限定从句，但值得重点讲解。
sentences.paraphrase: The first ballad sold very well because the event was recent and had attracted much attention.

reuse.zh: 我们在外面讨论，因为天气很好。
reuse.en: We discussed it outside, the weather being fine.
reuse.note: 独立主格 weather being fine 有自己的逻辑主语，不是悬垂分词。

pdfNotes.title: 主动的 sold 与独立主格
pdfNotes.text: The first sold wonderfully 的 sold 是不及物用法，表示第一首诗销路很好。the event being recent, having made a great noise 是带自己逻辑主语 event 的分词补充结构；新近发生并引起轰动的是事件，而非诗歌的艺术成就。

sentences.text: This flattered my vanity; but my father discouraged me by ridiculing my performances, and telling me verse-makers were generally beggars.
sentences.translation: 这满足了我的虚荣心；但父亲嘲笑我的作品，并说写诗的人通常都是乞丐，打消了我的热情。

classification.label: 并列复合句
classification.reason: 同时包含主句之间的并列以及内部或附加的限定从句。
classification.note: by 后两个 -ing 并列。telling me 后省略 that；beggars 是父亲关于生计的概括，不能在语义卡里变为作者给所有诗人的客观定义。

sentences.note: by 后两个 -ing 并列。telling me 后省略 that；beggars 是父亲关于生计的概括，不能在语义卡里变为作者给所有诗人的客观定义。
sentences.paraphrase: The success pleased my vanity, but my father mocked the poems and warned that poets usually ended up poor.

reuse.zh: 他指出风险并解释困难，使我打消了这个念头。
reuse.en: He discouraged me by pointing out the risks and explaining the difficulties.
reuse.note: by 后两个 doing 并列，不把第二项改为 to do。

pdfNotes.title: vanity 和 beggars 的语气
pdfNotes.text: flattered my vanity 是满足了我的虚荣心，不是有人向我谄媚。beggars 是乞丐，父亲借此说写诗难以维生；讲义 pathetic 不能完整替代这个经济处境。父亲的说法是人物意见，不是“诗人全都贫穷”的事实定义。

sentences.text: So I escaped being a poet, most probably a very bad one; but as prose writing had been of great use to me in the course of my life, and was a principal means of my advancement, I shall tell you how, in such a situation, I acquired what little ability I have in that way.
sentences.translation: 这样我便免于当一个诗人——多半还会是个很差的诗人。不过散文写作一生给了我很大帮助，也是我进步的重要途径，所以我要说说，在那样的处境下，我是怎样学到仅有的这点写作本领的。

classification.label: 并列复合句
classification.reason: 同时包含主句之间的并列以及内部或附加的限定从句。
classification.note: escape 后接 doing。as 是因为；how 从句为 tell 的内容。what little ability 表示“仅有的那点能力”，I have 是修饰 ability 的关系从句，不把 what 理解为询问什么能力。

clauses: most probably a very bad one
as prose writing had been … and was …
how … I acquired what little ability I have …
what little ability I have in that way 作 acquired 的宾语
functions: most probably a very bad one;
as prose writing had been of great use to me in the course of my life, and was a principal means of my advancement,
what little ability I have in that way.
sentences.note: what little ability I have in that way 是融合关系结构，整体作 acquired 的宾语；不机械恢复成“先行词 + 普通定语从句”。
sentences.paraphrase: I therefore avoided becoming a probably poor poet. Since prose helped my later progress, I will explain how I developed my limited writing ability.

reuse.pattern: As ___ has been useful to me, I will explain how ___.
reuse.zh: 因为这种方法对我有用，我会解释我是如何使用它的。
reuse.en: As this method has been useful to me, I will explain how I use it.
reuse.note: as 表原因，how 从句作 explain 的宾语。

pdfNotes.title: prose 与 acquire 不应套绝对规则
pdfNotes.text: prose 是非诗体的普通行文，范围比中文文学体裁“散文”更广。acquire 能指逐渐习得技能，也能指购得财物；obtain 也能接知识、许可等抽象事物，不能硬分成“acquire 必须长期、obtain 必须立即”。

sentences.text: There was another bookish lad in the town, John Collins by name, with whom I was intimately acquainted.
sentences.translation: 镇上还有个爱读书的少年，名叫约翰·柯林斯，我与他很熟。

classification.label: 主从复合句
classification.reason: 主句带有限定从句；按主干、从属关系和内部成分逐层拆解。
classification.note: with 来自 be acquainted with somebody；which 不能代人，此处用 whom。若现代改成 know，须说 whom I knew well，不保留 with。

clauses: There was another bookish lad in the town
with whom I was intimately acquainted
functions: with whom I was intimately acquainted.
sentences.note: with 来自 be acquainted with somebody；which 不能代人，此处用 whom。若现代改成 know，须说 whom I knew well，不保留 with。
sentences.paraphrase: Another keen reader in town was John Collins, whom I knew well.

reuse.zh: 班里有一位同学，我经常和她讨论书籍。
reuse.en: There was a classmate with whom I often discussed books.
reuse.note: with whom 来自 discuss books with somebody；不能写 with whom I knew。

pdfNotes.title: know 和 acquainted 的介词差别
pdfNotes.text: 原文 with whom I was intimately acquainted 正确：be acquainted with somebody。讲义改写 with whom I knew well 多了 with；应写 whom I knew well，或保留 with whom I was well acquainted。

sentences.text: We sometimes disputed, and very fond we were of argument, and very desirous of confuting one another, which disputatious turn, by the way, is apt to become a very bad habit, making people often extremely disagreeable in company by the contradiction that is necessary to bring it into practice; and thence, besides souring and spoiling the conversation, is productive of disgusts and, perhaps enmities where you may have occasion for friendship.
sentences.translation: 我们有时争辩，而且很爱争论，急于驳倒对方。顺便说，这种好辩的习性很容易变成坏习惯：实践它就得不断反驳别人，使人在交往中十分讨嫌；它还会弄坏谈话气氛，招致反感甚至仇怨，而那些场合你或许正需要友谊。

classification.label: 并列复合句
classification.reason: 同时包含主句之间的并列以及内部或附加的限定从句。
classification.note: 前置的是 very fond，we were 次序不变。which disputatious turn 是关系限定词加名词的旧式回指；is productive 仍与 is apt 共用 turn，不能因分号断错层级。making people disagreeable 是宾语加宾补。

clauses: very fond we were of argument, and (were) very desirous …
which disputatious turn … is apt … and … is productive …
that is necessary … 修饰 contradiction
where you may have occasion for friendship
functions: and very desirous of confuting one another,
is apt to become a very bad habit,
making people often extremely disagreeable in company
that is necessary to bring it into practice;
besides souring and spoiling the conversation,
is productive of disgusts and, perhaps enmities
where you may have occasion for friendship.
sentences.note: 前置的是 very fond，we were 次序不变。which disputatious turn 是关系限定词加名词的旧式回指；is productive 仍与 is apt 共用 turn，不能因分号断错层级。making people disagreeable 是宾语加宾补。
sentences.paraphrase: We loved trying to defeat each other's arguments, a habit that can make social life unpleasant and create hostility where friendship would be useful.

reuse.zh: 不断打断别人会伤害友谊，也容易成为习惯。
reuse.en: Constantly interrupting others, which can harm friendships, is apt to become a habit.
reuse.note: 用现代 which 从句表达后果，不要求照搬 which disputatious turn 的旧式结构。

pdfNotes.title: 表语前置与长定语从句
pdfNotes.text: very fond we were 是表语 very fond 前置，主语 we 仍在 were 前面，不能叫主谓倒装。which disputatious turn 是旧式“关系限定词 which + 名词”，回指好争辩的习性；is apt 和 is productive 共用这个从句主语，分号不意味着后者另起主句。

pdfNotes.title: 反思好辩，不是给群体下定论
pdfNotes.text: in company 指社交场合；catch it 是染上前述习惯。作者把律师、大学人士和在爱丁堡受培养的人列为例外，带讽刺和时代偏见，不能将其整理成关于职业或国籍的客观常识。

sentences.text: I had caught it by reading my father's books of dispute about religion.
sentences.translation: 我是读父亲那些关于宗教论辩的书，才染上这种习惯的。

classification.label: 简单句
classification.reason: 一个展开的限定主句；共用主语的并列谓语、非谓语或缩略表达另作提示。
classification.note: 过去完成时 had caught 把习惯来源追溯到前述争论之前。it 回指好辩习性，不指一本书；by reading 是介词加非谓语。

sentences.text: But I found I wanted a stock of words, or a readiness in recollecting and using them, which I thought I should have acquired before that time if I had gone on making verses; since the continual occasion for words of the same import, but of different length, to suit the measure, or of different sound for the rhyme, would have laid me under a constant necessity of searching for variety, and also have tended to fix that variety in my mind, and make me master of it.
sentences.translation: 但我发现自己缺少词汇储备，或者说，缺少迅速想起并运用词语的本领。我想若此前一直写诗，这时本来就会掌握这些能力：诗歌总要求为了格律和韵脚，寻找意思相同而长度或读音不同的词，这本会迫使我不断搜寻不同表达，也会使这些表达牢牢记在脑中，让我掌握它们。

classification.note: 这是多层嵌套的重点句。which 为 acquired 的宾语，穿过 I thought 的报告层。I should have 是旧式第一人称反事实“本会”，不是责备；since 是因为，would 与后面 have tended 共用。make me master 是宾语＋名词宾补。

clauses: (that) I wanted a stock of words, or a readiness …
which I thought I should have acquired …
if I had gone on making verses
since the continual occasion … would have laid … and also have tended …
functions: a stock of words, or a readiness in recollecting and using them,
which I thought I should have acquired before that time
if I had gone on making verses;
the continual occasion for words of the same import, but of different length, to suit the measure, or of different sound for the rhyme,
under a constant necessity of searching for variety,
to fix that variety in my mind,
and make me master of it.
sentences.note: which 对应 acquired 的宾语位置，穿过 I thought 的报告层；I should have acquired … 应单独列为 thought 的宾语从句。
sentences.paraphrase: I lacked vocabulary or ease in using it. Continuing with poetry might have built those skills, since metre and rhyme would have forced me to find and remember alternative words.

reuse.pattern: If I had ___, I would have ___.
reuse.zh: 如果我坚持练习，本来会变得更熟练。
reuse.en: If I had kept practising, I would have become more proficient.
reuse.note: 对过去的反事实；用现代 would have 迁移原文 I should have。

pdfNotes.title: 过去反事实中的 should 与 would
pdfNotes.text: I found 后省略 that；wanted 在此是缺少。which I thought I should have acquired 中 which 是 acquired 的宾语，I thought 是嵌入报告层。if I had gone on… 是与过去事实相反的条件；第一人称 I should have 在这里相当于 I would have，不是“我本来有义务”。since 引出原因，would have laid 与 would also have tended 共享虚拟前提。

pdfNotes.title: 同义选词、格律和韵脚
pdfNotes.text: same import 指意思相同，different length 配合诗行格律；different sound 指从意义相近的候选词中改选合适读音，以与别处韵脚呼应，不是说押韵词的韵尾必须不同。readiness 是迅速调用词语的熟练程度，不单指乐意。

sentences.text: Therefore I took some of the tales and turned them into verse; and, after a time, when I had pretty well forgotten the prose, turned them back again.
sentences.translation: 因此我选了些故事改成诗，过一段时间，等原来的散文体文字几乎忘了，再把它们改回去。

sentences.text: I also sometimes jumbled my collections of hints into confusion, and after some weeks endeavored to reduce them into the best order, before I began to form the full sentences and complete the paper.

reuse.en: Before I began to write, I arranged my notes in a logical order.
reuse.note: arrange…in order 是现代自然表达，不照搬 reduce…into order。

sentences.text: By comparing my work afterward with the original, I discovered many faults and amended them; but I sometimes had the pleasure of fancying that, in certain particulars of small import, I had been lucky enough to improve the method or the language, and this encouraged me to think I might possibly in time come to be a tolerable English writer, of which I was extremely ambitious.
sentences.translation: 后来与原文比较，我发现并改了许多毛病；但有时也会高兴地觉得，在某些无关紧要的细节上，我碰巧把组织或措辞改善了一点。这鼓励我相信，也许终有一天我能成为一个还算像样的英语写作者，而这正是我热切追求的目标。

classification.label: 并列复合句
classification.reason: 同时包含主句之间的并列以及内部或附加的限定从句。
classification.note: 三条主句加多层内容从句。of which 指成为写作者这一目标；旧式 ambitious of 不宜当现代默认搭配。fancying、possibly、small import 与 tolerable 限定自评，不等于断言自己已超越原作。

clauses: I discovered many faults and amended them
I sometimes had the pleasure of fancying …
that … I had been lucky enough to improve …
of which I was extremely ambitious
functions: By comparing my work afterward with the original,
that, in certain particulars of small import, I had been lucky enough to improve the method or the language,
I might possibly in time come to be a tolerable English writer,
of which I was extremely ambitious.
sentences.note: 三条主句加多层内容从句。of which 指成为写作者这一目标；旧式 ambitious of 不宜当现代默认搭配。fancying、possibly、small import 与 tolerable 限定自评，不等于断言自己已超越原作。
sentences.paraphrase: Comparing versions helped me correct errors. Occasionally I thought I had improved a minor detail, which encouraged my hope of becoming a competent writer.

reuse.pattern: ___ encouraged me to think that I might ___.
reuse.zh: 这次小小的成功让我觉得，我也许最终能写得更好。
reuse.en: This small success encouraged me to think that I might eventually write better.
reuse.note: encourage + 宾语 + to do；might 保留可能性，不能改成必然会。

pdfNotes.title: 谦逊表达不等于已经超越原作
pdfNotes.text: fancying、in certain particulars、of small import、lucky、might possibly 和 tolerable 层层限制判断：只是觉得某些小处也许有所改进。of which I was ambitious 中 which 回指成为合格写作者的目标，旧式 ambitious of 可现代改写为 eager to achieve that goal。

sentences.text: My time for these exercises and for reading was at night, after work or before it began in the morning, or on Sundays, when I contrived to be in the printing-house alone, evading as much as I could the common attendance on public worship which my father used to exact on me when I was under his care, and which indeed I still thought a duty, though I could not, as it seemed to me, afford time to practice it.
sentences.translation: 我只能在晚上、下工后或早晨开工前，以及星期日读书练习。周日我设法独自留在印刷所，尽量不参加日常的集体礼拜；从前受父亲管束时，他要求我参加。我其实仍认为这是职责，只是觉得实在抽不出时间。

classification.reason: 主句带有限定从句；按主干、从属关系和内部成分逐层拆解。
classification.note: 两个 which 都修饰 attendance，第二个作 thought 的宾语、a duty 为宾补。evading 主语是 I，不是 My time。最后 it 指参加礼拜这一实践；原文未明确每次都同父亲一起去。
